title: Allocation-lock timeout hint must report the break file alloc.lock.break and stop calling alloc.lock safe to remove unconditionally
description: Follow-up from the QCLI-495 narrow review (team-lead, opum-doc earlier ruling: a named error showing the exact file, never auto-clearing). The timeout hint in src/cli/main.ts (the IdAllocationLockTimeoutError branch, about :4809-4819) never mentions <common-dir>/quest/alloc.lock.break. A break file left by a breaker killed between creating and writing it is never auto-cleared (unreadable pid), blocks breaking a stale alloc.lock, and today the hint says removing alloc.lock is safe, which is wrong while a live break holder exists. Not started.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The allocation-lock timeout hint reports whether alloc.lock.break is present and its holder (the pid, or the word unreadable).
The hint says removing alloc.lock is safe only when there is no live break holder, and names the exact break file path when one exists.

The hint never removes or clears the break file by itself; a test fixture with a live-pid break file and one with an unreadable break file each assert the hint text, and the test goes red when the break-file clause is removed.

plan: 1. Read the task and the QCLI-495 allocator: the timeout error carries the lock path, holder pid and age but nothing about alloc.lock.break, and the hint in main.ts calls the lock safe to remove unconditionally.

2. Extend IdAllocationLockTimeoutError with breakPath, breakFilePresent, breakHolderPid (null = unreadable) and breakHolderAlive, populated in acquireLock timeout branch from readLock on the break path.

3. Move the hint text into allocationLockTimeoutHint in the application layer so it is testable without a ten-second spawn; the three states are: absent, present with a LIVE holder (removal NOT safe), present with an unreadable or dead holder (blocks breaking a stale lock, name the file, never clear it).
4. main.ts uses the shared builder and adds breakPath/breakFilePresent/breakHolderPid to input.

5. Tests in test/qcli522-alloc-lock-break-hint.test.ts: three text assertions, plus two end-to-end fixtures in a real repo (live-pid break file; zero-byte break file beside a stale lock) asserting exit 5, the hint text and that the break file is left untouched.
6. Mutation control: remove the break clause and confirm the tests go red, then restore.
7. bun run check on bun 1.4.2, commit on fix/QCLI-522-alloc-break-hint, push, open the PR, report the head SHA.
implementationNotes: Evidence, 2026-10-21. allocationLockTimeoutHint now lives in src/application/tasks/id-allocation.ts so the text is assertable without the allocator ten-second window; the CLI calls it and echoes breakPath, breakFilePresent and breakHolderPid in input. Tests: 3 text cases (absent, LIVE holder, unreadable holder) plus 2 end-to-end fixtures in a real repository -- a live-pid break file (the test process own pid) and a zero-byte break file beside a genuinely stale lock (dead pid, stamp 60s old) -- both assert exit 5, the exact hint sentences and that the break file is left untouched. MUTATION CONTROL for AC3: emptying the break-file clause turned all five tests red (measured; every one of them asserts text inside that clause); restored, 5/5 pass and the two QCLI-495 allocator suites still pass 32/32. bun run check exits 0 on bun 1.4.2 (1271 tests, 0 fail).

Round-1 review fixes in 249d438a on fix/QCLI-522-alloc-break-hint. MAJOR-1: the hint no longer asserts a cause for an unreadable break holder -- it says the holder cannot be determined, names the possibilities without choosing one, and makes removal conditional on BOTH no quest process running AND the file being older than the break window; a second branch covers a file still inside the write window. breakFileAgeMilliseconds is carried on the error from breaker.at and on the wire as input.breakFileStampedMillisecondsAgo. MAJOR-2: the present-readable-pid-not-alive branch now has a text case and an e2e fixture (live lock held by the test own pid plus a dead break pid) asserting exit 5, the not-running wording and an untouched break file. MINOR 3: readLock returns null on ENOENT between the stat and the read, so a vanished file is absent, not unreadable. MINOR 4: the e2e temp root is realpath-ed. MINOR 5: the CHANGELOG bullet describes the break file and the new condition. NITs: the main.ts comment no longer claims the hint reports the wait, and holderGoneWhen says no process with pid N is running (existence only). The allocation guide repeated the same overclaim, so it was corrected too, beyond the review list.
MUTATION EVIDENCE, re-measured independently by the session that pushed: deleting the unreadable-holder branch gives 3 fail / 5 pass (both unreadable wording cases and the unreadable e2e); deleting the dead-holder branch gives 2 fail / 6 pass (the dead-pid text case and the dead-pid e2e); unmutated control 8 pass / 0 fail. Each mutant restored and verified byte-identical to HEAD.
CORRECTED REVIEW PREMISE, measured: MINOR 4 said the un-realpath-ed fixture fails on macOS. It does not fail there -- it passed for the wrong reason. The CLI reports /private/var/... while the fixture compared /var/..., and the assertion is toContain, a substring check, so /private/var/folders/... CONTAINS /var/folders/.... The realpath fix is still right; the comparison was accidentally true, not equal.
finalSummary: Delivered on fix/QCLI-522-alloc-break-hint. The allocation-lock timeout hint now reports <common-dir>/quest/alloc.lock.break: whether the file is present and, when it is, its holder as a pid or the word unreadable. It calls removing alloc.lock safe only when no live break holder exists, names the exact break-file path in every present case, and never removes or clears the file -- the wording and the code path only report it. The four new error fields (breakPath, breakFilePresent, breakHolderPid, breakHolderAlive) are populated from a read of the break file in the acquireLock timeout branch, and the hint text moved to allocationLockTimeoutHint in the application layer so it is testable without the ten-second spawn. Evidence: 3 text assertions and 2 real-repository end-to-end fixtures (live-pid break file; zero-byte break file beside a stale lock, break file left untouched), 5/5 pass; emptying the break-file clause turns all five red (mutation control), restored they pass and the QCLI-495 suites pass 32/32; bun run check exits 0 on bun 1.4.2 (1271 tests, 0 fail).
